//: EAS Build config for the Grub native app (Expo SDK 56). appVersionSource=remote is the recommended behaviour from EAS CLI 12+: EAS owns android.versionCode / ios.buildNumber, and autoIncrement (set per profile below) bumps them server-side. android.package is com.harding.meals_android_client (see app.json). NO credentials are configured here: signing comes from EAS-managed (remote) credentials, which is the default credentialsSource.

build.//: base is a shared profile the three real profiles extend; it is never built directly.

development.//: Dev client build for on-device debugging. distribution=internal yields a shareable install URL; requires the expo-dev-client package to be added before this profile will produce a usable client. Android ships as an installable APK; iOS targets the simulator so it needs no provisioning. ios.simulator builds are .app bundles for the iOS Simulator, not device installs.

preview.//: Internal / ad-hoc test build of the production app (no dev client). distribution=internal gives a shareable install link. Android is an installable APK. iOS uses ad-hoc enterpriseProvisioning so the .ipa installs on registered test devices — this still needs the provisioned bundle id + Apple team (see the production ios note).

production.//: Store builds for both platforms. Android produces an .aab (app-bundle) for Google Play. autoIncrement bumps the EAS-managed build numbers each run (pairs with cli.appVersionSource=remote).
production.//ios: iOS store build is NOT yet runnable: app.json still carries the placeholder bundleIdentifier com.harding.meals-ios-client. Before this profile can build, set a real provisioned iOS bundle id (and, for the share extension, its own bundle id + shared App Group) and supply the Apple Team ID — either via the eas.json submit.production.ios block or by letting EAS prompt for App Store Connect credentials. See app.config.js TODO(iOS provisioning).
